title: Nitrate and phosphate gave different oxygen budgets on P16N at sigma0 26.5 in 2006-2015
abstract: We tested whether oxygen loss on a proposed offshore source path of the California oxygen low fits fixed oxygen-to-nutrient budgets. We used joint flag-2 bottles from GLODAPv2.2023 near 152 W at 27-46 N. In 2006-2015, oxygen on sigma0 26.5 fell by 11.15 micromol/kg. Nitrate rose by 1.00 and phosphate rose by 0.166. NO = oxygen + (170/16) nitrate changed by -0.54, with a conditional 95% interval of -1.68 to +0.46. PO = oxygen + 170 phosphate rose by 17.06 (14.84 to 19.47). The upper minus 2000 m PO contrast rose by 16.10 (13.46 to 18.99). Its adverse lower limit was +1.65 under uniform cruise shifts of up to 1% oxygen and 2% phosphate. Additive cruise errors cancel in that contrast. The same calibration test failed at a 138:1 ratio, at a 1500 m reference and in some adjacent-surface tests. The strict bracket rule left too few common bins. In 1991-2015, both upper composites had intervals that included zero, so a long endpoint test can miss the intervening phosphate difference. The result constrains a fixed-property, fixed-ratio budget. It does not identify changed respiration, ventilation or source oxygen. Two-occupation sampling, chemical ratios, depth-dependent errors, mixing and sparse historical deep support limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, a figure and an independent arithmetic audit are included. External records remain outside the baseline package.

display.caption: Oxygen and nutrient-composite changes on P16N. Bars show conditional 95% latitude-block intervals. NO uses 170:16; PO uses 170:1. Calibration bounds are reported separately. Deep comparisons use different common-bin support.
